      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted in any form
for publication in OUTLETTERS:
BASIC PRINT or DATA; handwritten
or typed copy; all wordprocessor
files (please state which!) or a
simple JOTTER program is in our
Issue 2(Disk #4).The easiest for
us to edit are Tasword 2 files
with the right margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Graham Marshall, LEICS.


Dear Ron/Brian,

I am a serious Spectrum user who
would like to go 'on-line'and,as
I am also an electronics enthus-
iast, I am considering building
the MODEM project published in
the Feb. issue of "PRACTICAL
ELECTRONICS". I am not really
interested in MICRONET but main-
ly in bulletin boards and large
databases etc. However as I
understand it, I wold also need
an RS232 interface and proper
comms' software to drive it. So:

A) Where would I be able to ob-
tain these?

B) Would the setup be compatible
wth my +D and STAR LC10 enabling
me to up/download software,mess-
ages etc.?

I would be most grateful if you
could answer these questions and
interested to hear from anyone
who has a communications setup
or interested in buildng the
same MODEM.

            - Graham Marshall

To Graham Marshall from Brian


I know of no commercial, stand-
alone RS232 interface available
for the Spectrum. The Interface
1 RS232 and WAFADRIVE are non-
standard and not suitable for
modem work although I understand
that some enthusiasts on the
continent did have such a system
working in a limited way. In any
case,neither Interface 1 or WAFA
would work with your +D.

Although you say you are not
really interested in Micronet, I
would advise you to contact them
to see if they still offer a
free VTX5000 with each new
subscription and,if so, take out

a "once-only" sub. (about `23 I
believe). This will (a) give you
some experience in using a modem
(so if you do get your own hard-
ware up and running you would be
able to test it in a known
environment)but,more importantly
(b) you would be in touch with
many comms users who could help
and advise and (c) you could
download some comms software
that might be modified for your
own hardware.

Failing that, ask Micronet if
they would sell you a VTX5000 on
its own or buy one second-hand
from the classified ads. The
reason why I keep coming back to
the VTX5000 is that if you have
electronics knowledge it is

possible to modify it and use it
as an RS232. Micronet users in
the Spectrum area are a helpful
lot and you can often rapidly
find information. I don't think
you will get very far anywhere
else unless you are very lucky
and stumble by chance across one
of the few people in the world
who have a normal modem working
on a Spectrum.

It may be, of course,that one of
our own readers may see this and
be able to help.
                    - Brian

From Richard Tanswell, SUFFOLK

Dear Ron and Brian,

I'm a seventeen-year-old student
and hoping to go to university
this October. I have a Spectrum
128K +2 and would like to use
it to write reports on.Could you
please suggest a printer (quite
good quality but not too costly)
and a software utility I could
use.Also, do I need an interface
for the printer and can I use a
joystick or more importantly my
mouse while still having the
printer attached?

I saw advertised in the April
issue of OUTLET a machine code
compilation. Would this help/

teach absolute beginners of
machine code,like me,who haven't
a clue where to start? If not,do
you do a package or do you feel
it's best to learn by the book?

I would just like to also say
I think your drive magazine is
great and well worth the money,
even though , as a machine code
novice, I don't understand half
of it![Neither do I - B.C.] Keep
up the good work and thank you
for your time.

        Yours  sincerely,

          R.J. Tanswell

To Richard Tanswell from Brian

My first choice would be the
STAR LC10 printer which is very
popular and excellent value at
around `160. Check the adverts
in say, COMPUTER SHOPPER or
COMPUTER EXPRESS WEEKLY but make
sure that VAT is included. Also,
be aware that there is a colour
version (which you presumably do
not need) at around `30 to `40
more.

My second choice would be the
Citizen 120D at around `150-also
very good value.

Both machines use Epson standard
control codes and can be
connected to your +2's printer

port without needing any other
interface. Your mouse should not
cause any conflict.

As for software, I would go for
the wordprocessor, TASWORD PLUS
TWO,`19.95 from Tasman Software,
Springfield House, Hyde Terrace,
Leeds, LS2 9LN. This will enable
you to type reports, print them,
save them on tape, reload and
alter and edit them to your
hearts content. It will even let
you send in letters to OUTLET on
tape!

Yes,when I was checking my early
OUTCLASSES before compiling them
into OUTLET EXTRA 1, I looked to
see if anything wanted changing.
I have to admit in all modesty I

could find nothing to change and
I still think the first lesson
on machine code is the best
written anywhere to get novices
started. However, anyone who has
done a little BASIC programming
and knows some of the principles
would have an advantage. I can
fully recommend the compilation
EXTRA 1. An assembler is almost
essential as it enables you to
type machine commands directly
and it converts them to pure
code later. Assembling code
yourself is laborious and NO
professionals work without an
assembler. The good news is that
EXTRA 1 includes an assembler,
disassembler and debugging tool.
There is just no better value. I
paid as much for a single book

which confused me for months
before I bought another which
suddenly got me started on my
first little program.

Best of luck and remember, you
can always write in for help to
me or BoB Smith.
                    - Brian

From Mike Haine, Leamington Spa

Dear Eds.,

The SAM feature (OUTLET 31) was
a good start.I hope the ball can
be kept rolling. [Yes, but note
that,in future,some SAM-specific
articles may only be on the SAM
version of OUTLET - B.C.]

The following are some items
which may take the subject on a
bit. I have purposely left some
things in the air where I have,
to date, got stuck.

1. First is a bit of BASIC which
somewhat simplifies the process
of making SAM into a SPECTRUM.
It uses bits taken from FORMAT.

Let me say that I find Loading
progs from tape is perfect if
the output voltage from the
recorder is greater than about
0.3 volts. Mine gives just over
a volt and never misses. This
applies to CODE routines.

BASIC is not so easy, presumably
because of the headers (?) More
on that later.


A copy of the Spectrum ROM must
first be saved on tape together
with any other CODE progs which
one wants to run on SAM - in the
following,MONITOR (disassembler)
from PICTURESQUE and SAM's ROM
itself (for study!).

 10 REM "SPECROMLDR"
 20 LOAD "specrom" CODE 65536
 22 LOAD "mon16"  CODE  65536 +
25257
 24 LOAD "samrom" CODE 65536 +
32768
 25 FOR N = 1 TO 12  :  READ  X:
READ Y: POKE 66783,+X,Y : NEXT N
 30 POKE 65541,195,203,16 : POKE
50000,62,163,211,250,  62,4,211,
252,199
 40 CALL 50000
 50                         DATA
0,219,10,63,18,74,25,79,58,88,
64,92,79,66,92,79,162,147,177,
190,232,172,245,170

The m/c progs can be saved on
tape in the Spectrum and loaded
into SAM and then saved to disc.

"specromldr" is best typed into
SAM then saved on disc or tape.
Run Loads"specrom" and the other
M/c routines, pages in the next
page up leaving SAM running as a
Spectrum. This includes the key-
board so you must remember which
keys give Spectrum keywords. I
put my old rubber keyboard by my
side to remind me. If you try to
call Mon16 (USR 30479) nothing
happens because when page 2 is
paged in with specrom from add-
ress 0 it runs from that address
i.e. it resets the Spectrum. The
first part of its routine clears
RAM to FFFFh.Thus it clears the
code routines which were Loaded.
In fact,it does this by filling
addresses with"2"s then checks
and replaces them by zeros.

We can stop this by modifying
the ROM since it is now in RAM.
(Yes we can get rid of all those
old bugs too!). The mod needed
is a jump instruction to jump
over the RAM CLEAR routine. It
is poked in at the first poke in
line 30. (JP 4555)

M/c routines are now not lost
and RANDOMISE USR 30479 calls
the monitor and the SAM ROM or
any other code sequence can be
disassembled and listed.(or run
with the single step function
etc).

I have also loaded and run the
Assembler prog "EDITAS" this
way. Also one game (the only one
I have!).

2. BASIC PROGS. Once in Spectrum
mode all progs can be loaded
from tape and run in the usual
way. I am in fact writing this
on Tasword 2 in SAM.You may well
ask,"why then load progs in as
described in part 1?".The answer
is they can be loaded direct off
disc.

3. If one could page back to SAM
without loosing what is on the
higher pages. It should be easy
to use the disc to store text or
other data generated in Spectrum
mode. It surely must be possible
to do that, but I have failed to
sus out how as yet. OUT 250,x
takes one back to SAM, but the
memory banks are cleared in the
process. Any ideas?

4. It is possible to save BASIC
progs as CODE on tape and load
them in SAM as described above.
This is done by saving the BASIC
by:-

SAVE "name" CODE 23552,(PEEK
23641 + 256 * PEEK 23642- 23552)


This can then be loaded into SAM
and saved on disc and Loaded by:
30 LOAD "name" CODE 65536+ 23552
(Line 40 deleted of course).

The snag about this is running
of the "specrom" (on paging up)
resets system variables to their
initial values. I think this can
be got over by loading at some
higher address then moving them

down in Spectrum mode. With this
it would then be possible to
store all progs on disc and load
them into the Spectrum mode. ...
I feel sure it will be possible
to use the disc directly from
the Spectrum mode.
             Over to you!!!!!

                  Mike Haine

Thanks, Mike. I think the answer
is in a great emulator in this
(or next) month's SAM version of
OUTLET called EMUTILITY. It is
intended for games but enables
one to switch back and forth
easily between modes and one can
readily modify it (see the info
article).
                     - Brian

From Dave Tonks, WALSALL


        SAM COUPE UPDATE?

[Some of this is superceded by
events but worth reading!- B.C.]

Since the last time I wrote,I've
got a disc drive for the Sam.
When it arrived in early Febru-
ary, I excitedly unboxed it and
after plugging it in and doing
up the two screws, I started to
read the instruction book...

"Insert the Dos disc into drive
one", it said, "then press F9".

"Where's the DOS disc?", I
wondered.

Further investigation of the box
revealed the the DOS was not yet
ready, but would be sent as soon
as possibly. Well!! fancy a
company selling discs drives
with no DOS ready. I might as
well have put an ashtray in the
slot, for all the use the drive
was. Oh well, that's the price
you pay for buying a computer
that's only just hit the market.
Back to the trusty tape deck.

A FEW WEEKS GO BY....


At last, a DOS disc!!! Rush and
turn on the Sam. Insert the disc
in drive one, press F9, and...
nothing... Just a message on the
screen that says "NO DOS".

Of course there's a DOS you
stupid computer, I've just put
one in your drive!!!



Another delve into the envelope
finds a note explaining that
because of a "BUG in the ROM"
the computer is looking for the
DOS in the wrong place.When F9
is pressed the DOS is loaded
OK,but I must CALL it manually
with CALL 229385.


Right.. I've done that and the
Sam says OK. Put a blank disc in
the drive and type FORMAT.

After asking "ARE YOU SURE Y/N"
the Sam then proceeds to format
my disc. Whilst formatting,you
are kept up to date by a counter
at the bottom of the screen
telling you which track it's
formatting now. After this the
disc is automatically verified,
with the counter showing which
bit it's doing, and, if an error
occurs, which track it's on.

I finally have a drive that
works(after a bit of manual per-
suasion) and a blank formatted
disc. I'll now get some of the
programs I've written onto disc.

You must remember to type DEVICE
T before trying to load off tape
as the F9 key has also changed
the device to disc.

I load in a 40-odd K program off
tape and,after typing"DEVICE D",
save it to disc with SAVE"name".
Two or three whirrs and clicks
later, it comes up "OK". "That's
never saved all that to disc", I
think, so I type DIR and, sure
enough, the name is on the
directory. I don't believe that!
NEW the machine and go through
the DOS loading process again.

I now type LOAD "name", the disc
light comes on; the drive clicks
a couple of times and... there's
my program!I hate to have to say
it but the speed makes the Opus
look like a Wafadrive. Once they
get the ROM sorted out[Done!-See
later - B.C.]and DOS autoruns as
it should,it will be a very good
system.

I've found that if you type NEW
instead of hitting the reset
button,you don't have to load or
call the DOS again. The DOS can
hold 80 files which is reason-
able and the disc formats out to
780K. If you save off the DOS on
every disc,which is logical,this
takes 10K of your disc space.

There are some nice touches in
there, such as you can get an
ordinary directory on the screen
with DIR, or with DIR1 a version
with code starts/lengths and
BASIC autostarts printed out as
well. In this full directory,
each file is given a number, and
you can load any file, no matter
what type, by just typing LOAD n
where n= the number of the file
you want.

There are, of course, all the
normal LOAD, SAVE, ERASE,COPY
commands there, and a few extras
as well.You can HIDE a file from
the directory or save a
PROTECTED file which needs a
special command to overwrite it.

If you save a file with a name
that already exists, the machine
asks "OVERWRITE Y/N", which at
times gets to be a pain, but a
couple of times has stopped me
wiping a file out that I needed.
All in all, not a bad system to
live with.


Now a few bits and pieces on the
Sam itself.

First a small warning. There has
been a slight modification to
the Sam's construction - namely
the RESET and BREAK buttons on
the back.My machine had longish,
thin black buttons which always
seemed loose to the touch. They
protruded out of holes in the
case which seemed much too big
for them.

The other week I had a go with
the Spectrum emulator which MGT
supply. Having got a Spectrum
program into the Sam, I pressed
the button and the machine
crashed. I tried again, and this
time the button worked and froze
the program. I could then press
key 4 and the program was saved
to the Sam disc.

Over the next few days I managed
to get a few of my Spectrum
collection across to the Sam,
but the BREAK button was very
unreliable. Sometime it would
crash a program the first time,
and freeze it perfectly the
next. I finally traced this to
the button itself, which had to
be helds lightly up as it was
pressed, before it would work.
At about the same time as this,I
had a call from another Spectrum
Discovery Club member, who could
not get his button to work at
all. After seeing a recently-
bought Sam, I noticed MGT had
changed the button design. They
were now much more chunky and
had a much better feel to them.
I meant to phone MGT to question

about this but fate lent a hand
and my BREAK button flew apart
and disappeared into the Sam.

MGT were very good, and got me a
replacement within days. This
has the "new" type buttons on it
which work perfectly first time,
every time (up to yet).

[From what I've heard the main
problem with the original BREAK
switches is that they are simple
push-to-make switches that force
multiple interrupts which varies
with the time they are kept
depressed. The new switches make
only a fleeting contact whether
you press them quickly or hold
them in firmly so the interrupt-
handler doesn't get muddled -BC]

While on the subject of modifi-
cations, can anyone tell me if
the Sam re-organises its memory
when a 512K upgrade is used? I
know that the DOS goes to a
different location because of
the CALL address but does much
else change? The reason I ask is
that with the various emulators
and Spectrum ROMS that can be
loaded in, my Snapshot/Break
button performs well.If,however,
I put my upgrade in, the machine
just NEWs back to Sam BASIC if
it is pressed. If anyone can
throw any light on the subject,
I would be very grateful.

My other query is, has anyone
used the SOUND command yet? The
manual mentions it hardly at all

and the technical manual is not
much better. I've tried using it
with a few FOR/NEXTloops but
only managed a couple of bleeps
and squeaks and I don't really
know how I got those. If anybody
has figured it out can they tell
the rest of us tone-deaf people
how they did it?

Anyway I'll sit quietly here
tapping away on the keys,eagerly
awaiting my free ROM upgrade
pack. They said April but they
didn't say which year.
                   Dave Tonks

Sorry,Dave- I too, could make no
sense of SOUND and and would be
glad if anyone could write a few
procedures to bring it up from
low-level to high. - Brian.

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

    SAM DISC BOOT PROBLEMS of
   Bob Rutherford Outlet #33.

Although not said in the letter
but the fact that Bob has a copy
of the DOS on tape I presume he
is using an external drive via
interface with SAM.If this guess
is correct then I can confirm
that I also found it impossible
to BOOT SAM from the external
drive. Once booted it would read
and write to the drive o.k.
However,I had to resort to boot-
ing from tape.I also found that,
although the drive works fine
with a Disciple at a step rate
of 6mS when used with SAM this
had to be set nearer to 20mS.

Finally on this subject, I had
problems using a combination of
internal and external drives as
Sam sometimes became confused as
to which was drive 1 & 2. [Since
receiving this letter, The
problem should now be overcome
anyway because the new SAM ROM
has been issued.See later- B.C.]


          LC10 PRINTER.

Did you know that the code
CHR$(27);CHRS 0 does a print-out
of its DIP SWITCH SETTINGS? Also
in my handbook the code
CHRS(27);CHR$(12) is said to be
ignored with friction-feed
paper. However, I find it does 1
reverse line feed.

         SCART CONNECTOR

In reply to Raymond Hoy with his
query  on the SCART connector,
providing the set has the option
installed then pin 20 of the
connector is for composite video
input with the screen (earth)
connected to pin 17. Therefore
taking the video from the
Spectrum modulator as previously
described should work.

Hope these bits and pieces are
of interest.
               Malcolm Perry


They most certainly are! Thanks
Malcolm.
                 - Brian

SAM UPDATE from Brian to all.

Many future articles specific to
the SAM might only appear on the
SAM version of OUTLET(or perhaps
ADD-ENDERS) but the info in this
letter is relevant to Spectrum
users waiting on developments
regarding SAM bugs, tape-loading
etc.before buying a SAM.

As most SAM users should know,
the new ROM has now been issued
to present owners and fitted to
all new machines. Contact MGT if
you haven't received yours yet.

MGT decided in the end to send
the ROM microchip to present SAM
owners to fit themselves with an
option to have it fitted by a

dealer if the user wasn't happy
or confident enough to tackle it
themselves.The fitting instruct-
ions were very clear and precise
and I think they made the right
decision there.

At the time of writing, I have
only had the new ROM a few days
and so the following details are
not the result of exhaustive
tests - by this time next month,
some things may have resolved
themselves or some new serious
bug may have emerged. However, I
am fairly confident that nothing
major will reveal itself that
cannot be circumvented.

I'm delighted to report that all
serious bugs have been removed;

one or two quirks and oddities
remain and I found a bug that is
new to me (but someone tells me
it was present with the old ROM)
I'm hoping it can be cured with
a POKE as it may be just a flag
that's not being set properly.

I'll deal with that first.If you
load from tape or use DEVICE T,
LOAD "" and then ESC. and DEVICE
D, the BOOT command no longer
works either by pressing F9 or
by typing in BOOT. Instead, the
drive whirs and then the SAM
waits for a tape load. If you
then load from a drive using a
LOAD command, it seems to work
o.k. after,suggesting,as I said,
some flag has then been reset
correctly. Unfortunately, if you

do NOT do this then the SAM soon
locks up say, after typing a
couple of lines then using LIST.
Because of this I was not able
to use the keyboard long enough
to track down the cause!

This fault is absolutely
consistent and I can't believe
none of the MGT team are aware
of it after months of testing.If
anyone finds a cure please let
us know. Meanwhile, I suggest
you use LOAD "AUTO*" within
programs to exit to a boot file.

Before I look at lesser quirks
(sounds like birdwatching) lets
look at the positive aspects.The
SAM COUPE is now the ULTIMATE
Spectrum upgrade. It has some


stunning features which have
been overshadowed in the last
few months. Not only the potent
graphics, faster BASIC and extra
commands; not only the improved
keyboard, ultra-fast disc drives
and better add-on connection;not
only the vastly-improved sound
possibilities and screen display
but its the little things that
are a joy to a BASIC programmer:
Function keys - just hit ONE key
to RUN or LIST or CLS or BOOT.
Furthermore, you can redefine
them to your hearts content.
Instant edit by typing the line
number then pressing EDIT - what
a boon! TAB - giving instant
spacing where you want! Try half
a dozen on the end of END PROC
or RETURN to see how it helps

space out the listing. On the
Spectrum you need EXTENDED MODE,
6 key, DELETE for EACH TAB.
The BREAK button - giving escape
even from many machine code
crashes! - What a saviour!

In BASIC, KEYIN has tremendous
potential as does MEM$ and INSTR
searching. However, the crowning
glory of the BASIC are the
procedures which are ideally
implemented enabling you to
INSTANTLY CREATE NEW KEYWORDS AS
YOU GO ALONG! Try this...


10 SETUP
20 PRINTMENU
30 TESTKEY
40 HAVEAPARTY

Want a special print routine?
Just do SPECPRINT "TEXT" then
write a procedure to say, switch
in a different character set,
alter the INK colour, set up
double height, print your string
and then restore to normal! The
possibilities for the creative
programmer are enormous!

I feel more confident about tape
loading too now I have got used
to the levels although some
commercial Spectrum programs may
still be difficult.

If you have been thinking about
buying a SAM COUPE, don't delay
any longer! We have a Spectrum
emulator in this or next month's
OUTLET that will run most

Spectrum programs - stop them at
any time, save them to disc or
tape, or even ramdisc and should
easily be modified by BASIC to
say, save Tasword 2 textfiles to
disc or use the printer.

O.K. Now back to the quirks...

File copying with one drive will
fail in Mode 1 or 2. Solution:
use Mode 3 or 4.

FORMAT to "D2:" fails in Mode 1
or 2. Solution: Use Mode 3 or 4.

Tape loading fails if the PRINT
position reaches the bottom of
screen (e.g. when I transfer all
the OUTLET files from Spectrum!)
Solution: use SCROLL CLEAR.

DUMP and DUMP CHR$ need extra
code to be loaded but it's not
available to tape-users so you
can't use DUMP in programs you
share nor do MGT tell beginners
how to install it IN programs.

DUMP CHR$ is o.k.- but no better
than TEEDEE in OUTLET 33 (so you
may prefer to merge TEEDEE for
most applications).

DUMP is disappointing.All colour
screens I tried were printed as
unrecognizable black blobs as if
all colour but white is printed
as black.The one success I had
was with a black and white clip
art screen.GEEDEE (OUTLET 33) is
slow but gives better results.
Solution: Wait for a 3rd-party
DUMP - probably in OUTLET!

OVER 1 is as previously reported
in OUTLET. Solution: Regard it
as a Mode 1 command only for all
practical puposes.

The F7 function key at switch-on
still does not set Device T to
load off tape. Solution:redefine
the key in your most-used file.

DVAR 2,which holds Drive 2 data,
is one of which to be wary. I'm
told there is a horrible crash
on COUPEs with one drive if a
drive 2 command is used and DVAR
2 is set for 2 drives.Users with
one drive should remember this
if booting from an unknown disc.
I had assumed that BOOT checked
to see if dos was already loaded
but it does appear to load dos

every time you boot the auto
file. This means when you boot
from a new disc you lose any
drive variables. For example, if
you have your dos set for one
drive and contribute a program
on disc and I boot it in to look
at it then ten minutes later I
may suddenly find my drive 2 is
not working! The dos on OUTLET
discs is, and must be, set for
two drives because many programs
have an option to load data etc.
and I'm certainly not limiting
users with two drives to only
using one of them! For example,
CATLOADER (OUTLET 33) can move
files using one disc or two.
(Incidentally, the MGT disk,
although it detected I have two
drives, still only offered one-

drive copying when it came to
backing up the disc!). Which
reminds me,there is a routine in
that program to detect how many
drives are installed so perhaps
it might be wise to use it in
the OUTLET AUTO loader file.

There are obviously many things
to think about. Some OUTLET
programs already issued do not
work with the new ROM and I have
to test the lot to find out what
and why! It's a pity we have to

From Gordon Roberts

Doesn't POKE 23730/23731 move
RAMTOP (without clearing the
screen or variables)?

Yes but not the stack which is
just under RAMTOP and is the
main object of the exercise. The
stack holds register values and
return addresses and if you say,
moved RAMTOP down to 40000 using
your method then loaded 25000
bytes of code above it then the
code would overwrite the stack
which would still be at around
65360 and the computer would
crash. Changing 23730/1 is just

From Graham Marshall, LEICS.

Dear Ron/Brian,

I am a serious Spectrum user who would like to go 'on-line'and,as I am also an electronics enthus- iast, I am considering building the MODEM project published in the Feb. issue of "PRACTICAL ELECTRONICS". I am not really interested in MICRONET but main- ly in bulletin boards and large databases etc. However as I understand it, I wold also need an RS232 interface and proper comms' software to drive it. So:

A) Where would I be able to ob- tain these?

B) Would the setup be compatible wth my +D and STAR LC10 enabling me to up/download software,mess- ages etc.?

I would be most grateful if you could answer these questions and interested to hear from anyone who has a communications setup or interested in buildng the same MODEM.

- Graham Marshall

To Graham Marshall from Brian

I know of no commercial, stand- alone RS232 interface available for the Spectrum. The Interface 1 RS232 and WAFADRIVE are non- standard and not suitable for modem work although I understand that some enthusiasts on the continent did have such a system working in a limited way. In any case,neither Interface 1 or WAFA would work with your +D.

Although you say you are not really interested in Micronet, I would advise you to contact them to see if they still offer a free VTX5000 with each new subscription and,if so, take out

a "once-only" sub. (about `23 I believe). This will (a) give you some experience in using a modem (so if you do get your own hard- ware up and running you would be able to test it in a known environment)but,more importantly (b) you would be in touch with many comms users who could help and advise and (c) you could download some comms software that might be modified for your own hardware.

Failing that, ask Micronet if they would sell you a VTX5000 on its own or buy one second-hand from the classified ads. The reason why I keep coming back to the VTX5000 is that if you have electronics knowledge it is

possible to modify it and use it as an RS232. Micronet users in the Spectrum area are a helpful lot and you can often rapidly find information. I don't think you will get very far anywhere else unless you are very lucky and stumble by chance across one of the few people in the world who have a normal modem working on a Spectrum.

It may be, of course,that one of our own readers may see this and be able to help. - Brian

From Richard Tanswell, SUFFOLK

Dear Ron and Brian,

I'm a seventeen-year-old student and hoping to go to university this October. I have a Spectrum 128K +2 and would like to use it to write reports on.Could you please suggest a printer (quite good quality but not too costly) and a software utility I could use.Also, do I need an interface for the printer and can I use a joystick or more importantly my mouse while still having the printer attached?

I saw advertised in the April issue of OUTLET a machine code compilation. Would this help/

teach absolute beginners of machine code,like me,who haven't a clue where to start? If not,do you do a package or do you feel it's best to learn by the book?

I would just like to also say I think your drive magazine is great and well worth the money, even though , as a machine code novice, I don't understand half of it![Neither do I - B.C.] Keep up the good work and thank you for your time.

Yours  sincerely,

R.J. Tanswell

To Richard Tanswell from Brian

My first choice would be the STAR LC10 printer which is very popular and excellent value at around `160. Check the adverts in say, COMPUTER SHOPPER or COMPUTER EXPRESS WEEKLY but make sure that VAT is included. Also, be aware that there is a colour version (which you presumably do not need) at around `30 to `40 more.

My second choice would be the Citizen 120D at around `150-also very good value.

Both machines use Epson standard control codes and can be connected to your +2's printer

port without needing any other interface. Your mouse should not cause any conflict.

As for software, I would go for the wordprocessor, TASWORD PLUS TWO,`19.95 from Tasman Software, Springfield House, Hyde Terrace, Leeds, LS2 9LN. This will enable you to type reports, print them, save them on tape, reload and alter and edit them to your hearts content. It will even let you send in letters to OUTLET on tape!

Yes,when I was checking my early OUTCLASSES before compiling them into OUTLET EXTRA 1, I looked to see if anything wanted changing. I have to admit in all modesty I

could find nothing to change and I still think the first lesson on machine code is the best written anywhere to get novices started. However, anyone who has done a little BASIC programming and knows some of the principles would have an advantage. I can fully recommend the compilation EXTRA 1. An assembler is almost essential as it enables you to type machine commands directly and it converts them to pure code later. Assembling code yourself is laborious and NO professionals work without an assembler. The good news is that EXTRA 1 includes an assembler, disassembler and debugging tool. There is just no better value. I paid as much for a single book

which confused me for months before I bought another which suddenly got me started on my first little program.

Best of luck and remember, you can always write in for help to me or BoB Smith. - Brian

From Mike Haine, Leamington Spa

Dear Eds.,

The SAM feature (OUTLET 31) was a good start.I hope the ball can be kept rolling. [Yes, but note that,in future,some SAM-specific articles may only be on the SAM version of OUTLET - B.C.]

The following are some items which may take the subject on a bit. I have purposely left some things in the air where I have, to date, got stuck.

1. First is a bit of BASIC which somewhat simplifies the process of making SAM into a SPECTRUM. It uses bits taken from FORMAT.

Let me say that I find Loading progs from tape is perfect if the output voltage from the recorder is greater than about 0.3 volts. Mine gives just over a volt and never misses. This applies to CODE routines.

BASIC is not so easy, presumably because of the headers (?) More on that later.

A copy of the Spectrum ROM must first be saved on tape together with any other CODE progs which one wants to run on SAM - in the following,MONITOR (disassembler) from PICTURESQUE and SAM's ROM itself (for study!).

10 REM "SPECROMLDR" 20 LOAD "specrom" CODE 65536 22 LOAD "mon16"  CODE  65536 + 25257 24 LOAD "samrom" CODE 65536 + 32768 25 FOR N = 1 TO 12  :  READ  X: READ Y: POKE 66783,+X,Y : NEXT N 30 POKE 65541,195,203,16 : POKE

```text
50000,62,163,211,250,  62,4,211,
```

252,199 40 CALL 50000

```text
 50                         DATA
0,219,10,63,18,74,25,79,58,88,
64,92,79,66,92,79,162,147,177,
190,232,172,245,170
```

The m/c progs can be saved on tape in the Spectrum and loaded into SAM and then saved to disc.

"specromldr" is best typed into SAM then saved on disc or tape. Run Loads"specrom" and the other M/c routines, pages in the next page up leaving SAM running as a Spectrum. This includes the key- board so you must remember which keys give Spectrum keywords. I put my old rubber keyboard by my side to remind me. If you try to call Mon16 (USR 30479) nothing happens because when page 2 is paged in with specrom from add- ress 0 it runs from that address i.e. it resets the Spectrum. The first part of its routine clears RAM to FFFFh.Thus it clears the code routines which were Loaded. In fact,it does this by filling addresses with"2"s then checks and replaces them by zeros.

We can stop this by modifying the ROM since it is now in RAM. (Yes we can get rid of all those old bugs too!). The mod needed is a jump instruction to jump over the RAM CLEAR routine. It is poked in at the first poke in line 30. (JP 4555)

M/c routines are now not lost and RANDOMISE USR 30479 calls the monitor and the SAM ROM or any other code sequence can be disassembled and listed.(or run with the single step function etc).

I have also loaded and run the Assembler prog "EDITAS" this way. Also one game (the only one I have!).

2. BASIC PROGS. Once in Spectrum mode all progs can be loaded from tape and run in the usual way. I am in fact writing this on Tasword 2 in SAM.You may well ask,"why then load progs in as described in part 1?".The answer is they can be loaded direct off disc.

3. If one could page back to SAM without loosing what is on the higher pages. It should be easy to use the disc to store text or other data generated in Spectrum mode. It surely must be possible to do that, but I have failed to sus out how as yet. OUT 250,x takes one back to SAM, but the memory banks are cleared in the process. Any ideas?

4. It is possible to save BASIC progs as CODE on tape and load them in SAM as described above. This is done by saving the BASIC by:-

SAVE "name" CODE 23552,(PEEK

```text
23641 + 256 * PEEK 23642- 23552)
```

This can then be loaded into SAM and saved on disc and Loaded by: 30 LOAD "name" CODE 65536+ 23552 (Line 40 deleted of course).

The snag about this is running of the "specrom" (on paging up) resets system variables to their initial values. I think this can be got over by loading at some higher address then moving them

down in Spectrum mode. With this it would then be possible to store all progs on disc and load them into the Spectrum mode. ... I feel sure it will be possible to use the disc directly from the Spectrum mode. Over to you!!!!!

Mike Haine

Thanks, Mike. I think the answer is in a great emulator in this (or next) month's SAM version of OUTLET called EMUTILITY. It is intended for games but enables one to switch back and forth easily between modes and one can readily modify it (see the info article). - Brian

From Dave Tonks, WALSALL

SAM COUPE UPDATE?

[Some of this is superceded by events but worth reading!- B.C.]

Since the last time I wrote,I've got a disc drive for the Sam. When it arrived in early Febru- ary, I excitedly unboxed it and after plugging it in and doing up the two screws, I started to read the instruction book...

"Insert the Dos disc into drive one", it said, "then press F9".

"Where's the DOS disc?", I wondered.

Further investigation of the box revealed the the DOS was not yet ready, but would be sent as soon as possibly. Well!! fancy a company selling discs drives with no DOS ready. I might as well have put an ashtray in the slot, for all the use the drive was. Oh well, that's the price you pay for buying a computer that's only just hit the market. Back to the trusty tape deck.

A FEW WEEKS GO BY....

At last, a DOS disc!!! Rush and turn on the Sam. Insert the disc in drive one, press F9, and... nothing... Just a message on the screen that says "NO DOS".

Of course there's a DOS you stupid computer, I've just put one in your drive!!!

Another delve into the envelope finds a note explaining that because of a "BUG in the ROM" the computer is looking for the DOS in the wrong place.When F9 is pressed the DOS is loaded OK,but I must CALL it manually with CALL 229385.

Right.. I've done that and the Sam says OK. Put a blank disc in the drive and type FORMAT.

After asking "ARE YOU SURE Y/N" the Sam then proceeds to format my disc. Whilst formatting,you are kept up to date by a counter at the bottom of the screen telling you which track it's formatting now. After this the disc is automatically verified, with the counter showing which bit it's doing, and, if an error occurs, which track it's on.

I finally have a drive that works(after a bit of manual per- suasion) and a blank formatted disc. I'll now get some of the programs I've written onto disc.

You must remember to type DEVICE T before trying to load off tape as the F9 key has also changed the device to disc.

I load in a 40-odd K program off tape and,after typing"DEVICE D", save it to disc with SAVE"name". Two or three whirrs and clicks later, it comes up "OK". "That's never saved all that to disc", I think, so I type DIR and, sure enough, the name is on the directory. I don't believe that! NEW the machine and go through the DOS loading process again.

I now type LOAD "name", the disc light comes on; the drive clicks a couple of times and... there's my program!I hate to have to say it but the speed makes the Opus look like a Wafadrive. Once they get the ROM sorted out[Done!-See later - B.C.]and DOS autoruns as it should,it will be a very good system.

I've found that if you type NEW instead of hitting the reset button,you don't have to load or call the DOS again. The DOS can hold 80 files which is reason- able and the disc formats out to 780K. If you save off the DOS on every disc,which is logical,this takes 10K of your disc space.

There are some nice touches in there, such as you can get an ordinary directory on the screen with DIR, or with DIR1 a version with code starts/lengths and BASIC autostarts printed out as well. In this full directory, each file is given a number, and you can load any file, no matter what type, by just typing LOAD n where n= the number of the file you want.

There are, of course, all the normal LOAD, SAVE, ERASE,COPY commands there, and a few extras as well.You can HIDE a file from the directory or save a PROTECTED file which needs a special command to overwrite it.

If you save a file with a name that already exists, the machine asks "OVERWRITE Y/N", which at times gets to be a pain, but a couple of times has stopped me wiping a file out that I needed. All in all, not a bad system to live with.

Now a few bits and pieces on the Sam itself.

First a small warning. There has been a slight modification to the Sam's construction - namely the RESET and BREAK buttons on the back.My machine had longish, thin black buttons which always seemed loose to the touch. They protruded out of holes in the case which seemed much too big for them.

The other week I had a go with the Spectrum emulator which MGT supply. Having got a Spectrum program into the Sam, I pressed the button and the machine crashed. I tried again, and this time the button worked and froze the program. I could then press key 4 and the program was saved to the Sam disc.

Over the next few days I managed to get a few of my Spectrum collection across to the Sam, but the BREAK button was very unreliable. Sometime it would crash a program the first time, and freeze it perfectly the next. I finally traced this to the button itself, which had to be helds lightly up as it was pressed, before it would work. At about the same time as this,I had a call from another Spectrum Discovery Club member, who could not get his button to work at all. After seeing a recently- bought Sam, I noticed MGT had changed the button design. They were now much more chunky and had a much better feel to them. I meant to phone MGT to question

about this but fate lent a hand and my BREAK button flew apart and disappeared into the Sam.

MGT were very good, and got me a replacement within days. This has the "new" type buttons on it which work perfectly first time, every time (up to yet).

[From what I've heard the main problem with the original BREAK switches is that they are simple push-to-make switches that force multiple interrupts which varies with the time they are kept depressed. The new switches make only a fleeting contact whether you press them quickly or hold them in firmly so the interrupt- handler doesn't get muddled -BC]

While on the subject of modifi- cations, can anyone tell me if the Sam re-organises its memory when a 512K upgrade is used? I know that the DOS goes to a different location because of the CALL address but does much else change? The reason I ask is that with the various emulators and Spectrum ROMS that can be loaded in, my Snapshot/Break button performs well.If,however, I put my upgrade in, the machine just NEWs back to Sam BASIC if it is pressed. If anyone can throw any light on the subject, I would be very grateful.

My other query is, has anyone used the SOUND command yet? The manual mentions it hardly at all

and the technical manual is not much better. I've tried using it with a few FOR/NEXTloops but only managed a couple of bleeps and squeaks and I don't really know how I got those. If anybody has figured it out can they tell the rest of us tone-deaf people how they did it?

Anyway I'll sit quietly here tapping away on the keys,eagerly awaiting my free ROM upgrade pack. They said April but they didn't say which year. Dave Tonks

Sorry,Dave- I too, could make no sense of SOUND and and would be glad if anyone could write a few procedures to bring it up from low-level to high. - Brian.

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

SAM DISC BOOT PROBLEMS of Bob Rutherford Outlet #33.

Although not said in the letter but the fact that Bob has a copy of the DOS on tape I presume he is using an external drive via interface with SAM.If this guess is correct then I can confirm that I also found it impossible to BOOT SAM from the external drive. Once booted it would read and write to the drive o.k. However,I had to resort to boot- ing from tape.I also found that, although the drive works fine with a Disciple at a step rate of 6mS when used with SAM this had to be set nearer to 20mS.

Finally on this subject, I had problems using a combination of internal and external drives as Sam sometimes became confused as to which was drive 1 & 2. [Since receiving this letter, The problem should now be overcome anyway because the new SAM ROM has been issued.See later- B.C.]

LC10 PRINTER.

Did you know that the code CHR$(27);CHRS 0 does a print-out of its DIP SWITCH SETTINGS? Also in my handbook the code CHRS(27);CHR$(12) is said to be ignored with friction-feed paper. However, I find it does 1 reverse line feed.

SCART CONNECTOR

In reply to Raymond Hoy with his query  on the SCART connector, providing the set has the option installed then pin 20 of the connector is for composite video input with the screen (earth) connected to pin 17. Therefore taking the video from the Spectrum modulator as previously described should work.

Hope these bits and pieces are of interest. Malcolm Perry

They most certainly are! Thanks Malcolm. - Brian

SAM UPDATE from Brian to all.

Many future articles specific to the SAM might only appear on the SAM version of OUTLET(or perhaps ADD-ENDERS) but the info in this letter is relevant to Spectrum users waiting on developments regarding SAM bugs, tape-loading etc.before buying a SAM.

As most SAM users should know, the new ROM has now been issued to present owners and fitted to all new machines. Contact MGT if you haven't received yours yet.

MGT decided in the end to send the ROM microchip to present SAM owners to fit themselves with an option to have it fitted by a

dealer if the user wasn't happy or confident enough to tackle it themselves.The fitting instruct- ions were very clear and precise and I think they made the right decision there.

At the time of writing, I have only had the new ROM a few days and so the following details are not the result of exhaustive tests - by this time next month, some things may have resolved themselves or some new serious bug may have emerged. However, I am fairly confident that nothing major will reveal itself that cannot be circumvented.

I'm delighted to report that all serious bugs have been removed;

one or two quirks and oddities remain and I found a bug that is new to me (but someone tells me it was present with the old ROM) I'm hoping it can be cured with a POKE as it may be just a flag that's not being set properly.

I'll deal with that first.If you load from tape or use DEVICE T, LOAD "" and then ESC. and DEVICE D, the BOOT command no longer works either by pressing F9 or by typing in BOOT. Instead, the drive whirs and then the SAM waits for a tape load. If you then load from a drive using a LOAD command, it seems to work o.k. after,suggesting,as I said, some flag has then been reset correctly. Unfortunately, if you

do NOT do this then the SAM soon locks up say, after typing a couple of lines then using LIST. Because of this I was not able to use the keyboard long enough to track down the cause!

This fault is absolutely consistent and I can't believe none of the MGT team are aware of it after months of testing.If anyone finds a cure please let us know. Meanwhile, I suggest you use LOAD "AUTO*" within programs to exit to a boot file.

Before I look at lesser quirks (sounds like birdwatching) lets look at the positive aspects.The SAM COUPE is now the ULTIMATE Spectrum upgrade. It has some

stunning features which have been overshadowed in the last few months. Not only the potent graphics, faster BASIC and extra commands; not only the improved keyboard, ultra-fast disc drives and better add-on connection;not only the vastly-improved sound possibilities and screen display but its the little things that are a joy to a BASIC programmer: Function keys - just hit ONE key to RUN or LIST or CLS or BOOT. Furthermore, you can redefine them to your hearts content. Instant edit by typing the line number then pressing EDIT - what a boon! TAB - giving instant spacing where you want! Try half a dozen on the end of END PROC or RETURN to see how it helps

space out the listing. On the Spectrum you need EXTENDED MODE, 6 key, DELETE for EACH TAB. The BREAK button - giving escape even from many machine code crashes! - What a saviour!

In BASIC, KEYIN has tremendous potential as does MEM$ and INSTR searching. However, the crowning glory of the BASIC are the procedures which are ideally implemented enabling you to INSTANTLY CREATE NEW KEYWORDS AS YOU GO ALONG! Try this...

10 SETUP 20 PRINTMENU 30 TESTKEY 40 HAVEAPARTY

Want a special print routine? Just do SPECPRINT "TEXT" then write a procedure to say, switch in a different character set, alter the INK colour, set up double height, print your string and then restore to normal! The possibilities for the creative programmer are enormous!

I feel more confident about tape loading too now I have got used to the levels although some commercial Spectrum programs may still be difficult.

If you have been thinking about buying a SAM COUPE, don't delay any longer! We have a Spectrum emulator in this or next month's OUTLET that will run most

Spectrum programs - stop them at any time, save them to disc or tape, or even ramdisc and should easily be modified by BASIC to say, save Tasword 2 textfiles to disc or use the printer.

O.K. Now back to the quirks...

File copying with one drive will fail in Mode 1 or 2. Solution: use Mode 3 or 4.

FORMAT to "D2:" fails in Mode 1 or 2. Solution: Use Mode 3 or 4.

Tape loading fails if the PRINT position reaches the bottom of screen (e.g. when I transfer all the OUTLET files from Spectrum!) Solution: use SCROLL CLEAR.

DUMP and DUMP CHR$ need extra code to be loaded but it's not available to tape-users so you can't use DUMP in programs you share nor do MGT tell beginners how to install it IN programs.

DUMP CHR$ is o.k.- but no better than TEEDEE in OUTLET 33 (so you may prefer to merge TEEDEE for most applications).

DUMP is disappointing.All colour screens I tried were printed as unrecognizable black blobs as if all colour but white is printed as black.The one success I had was with a black and white clip art screen.GEEDEE (OUTLET 33) is slow but gives better results. Solution: Wait for a 3rd-party DUMP - probably in OUTLET!

OVER 1 is as previously reported in OUTLET. Solution: Regard it as a Mode 1 command only for all practical puposes.

The F7 function key at switch-on still does not set Device T to load off tape. Solution:redefine the key in your most-used file.

DVAR 2,which holds Drive 2 data, is one of which to be wary. I'm told there is a horrible crash on COUPEs with one drive if a drive 2 command is used and DVAR 2 is set for 2 drives.Users with one drive should remember this if booting from an unknown disc. I had assumed that BOOT checked to see if dos was already loaded but it does appear to load dos

every time you boot the auto file. This means when you boot from a new disc you lose any drive variables. For example, if you have your dos set for one drive and contribute a program on disc and I boot it in to look at it then ten minutes later I may suddenly find my drive 2 is not working! The dos on OUTLET discs is, and must be, set for two drives because many programs have an option to load data etc. and I'm certainly not limiting users with two drives to only using one of them! For example, CATLOADER (OUTLET 33) can move files using one disc or two. (Incidentally, the MGT disk, although it detected I have two drives, still only offered one-

drive copying when it came to backing up the disc!). Which reminds me,there is a routine in that program to detect how many drives are installed so perhaps it might be wise to use it in the OUTLET AUTO loader file.

There are obviously many things to think about. Some OUTLET programs already issued do not work with the new ROM and I have to test the lot to find out what and why! It's a pity we have to discover the repercussions for ourselves. Write in with any useful info you discover.

For example, the multi-palette SCREEN$ "pal$"(OUTLET 33), saved with the old dos and rom will

crash if loaded by the new rom and dos. I must remember to put a new version in this issue.

My brain gets confused switching between computers! It's bad enough when I find myself trying to DELETE with the TAB key on my SAM but the other day I tried to lean my wrists on a Spectrum and nearly fell on the floor.

```text
                        - Brian
```

From Gordon Roberts

Doesn't POKE 23730/23731 move RAMTOP (without clearing the screen or variables)?

Yes but not the stack which is just under RAMTOP and is the main object of the exercise. The stack holds register values and return addresses and if you say, moved RAMTOP down to 40000 using your method then loaded 25000 bytes of code above it then the code would overwrite the stack which would still be at around 65360 and the computer would crash. Changing 23730/1 is just part of our CLEARCUT routine which works fine - but NOT on a +3 as is wanted.

```text
                        - Brian
```

From J. Fallows

Dear Ron & Brian,

I wonder if you could tell me if there is a program available to repair corrupted +3 discs. Quite often when loading I get"missing address mark" and I have to re- FORMAT the disc. Is there a way to get back the lost files?

Yours sincerely,

J. Fallows

To Mr. J. Fallows from Brian

There's PLUS-3 MATE, `12.99 from LERM, 11 Beaconsfield Close, Whitley Bay, Tyne and Wear, NE25 9UW (Tel:091 2533615) or DICE, `12.95 from KOBRAHSOFT, Pleasant View, Hulme Lane, Longton,Stoke- on-Trent, Staffs, ST3 5BH (this was reviewed in OUTLET 30).

If either of those can enable you to recover some files from a disc which is otherwise totally inaccessible they may be worth- while for your purposes.However, to repair individual files,other than pure text files, I do not have much faith in such programs since a machine code or BASIC program with only a few lost

bytes needs a lot of skill, time and effort to re-build and may often be impossible. I always recommend a back-up of every disc and then just duplicate the back-up and discard an original if it fails.

If you try one of the above disc repair programs I'd be very interested to hear if SOME files can be recovered from a totally inaccessible disc. If you get PLUS-3 MATE why not send us a review(must be a text file,PRINT or DATA - not hand-written or printed) and recover some of the cost?

```text
                       - Brian.
```

1. Для начала — небольшой фрагмент на BASIC, который несколько упрощает превращение SAM в SPECTRUM. В нем использованы наработки из FORMAT.

Замечу, что загрузка программ с ленты работает идеально, если выходное напряжение с магнитофона превышает примерно 0.3 вольта. Мой выдает чуть больше одного вольта и ни разу не дает сбоев. Это касается CODE-блоков.

С BASIC все не так просто, видимо, из-за заголовков (?) Но об этом позже.

Копию ROM Spectrum необходимо предварительно сохранить на ленту вместе с другими CODE-программами, которые вы хотите запустить на SAM — в данном случае это MONITOR (дизассемблер) от PICTURESQUE и собственный ROM SAM (для изучения!).

```text
 10 REM "SPECROMLDR"
 20 LOAD "specrom" CODE 65536
 22 LOAD "mon16"  CODE  65536 + 25257
 24 LOAD "samrom" CODE 65536 + 32768
 25 FOR N = 1 TO 12  :  READ  X: READ Y: POKE 66783,+X,Y : NEXT N
 30 POKE 65541,195,203,16 : POKE 50000,62,163,211,250,  62,4,211, 252,199
 40 CALL 50000
 50                         DATA 0,219,10,63,18,74,25,79,58,88, 64,92,79,66,92,79,162,147,177, 190,232,172,245,170
```

Программы в машинном коде можно сохранить на ленту на Spectrum, загрузить в SAM, а затем сохранить на диск.

«specromldr» лучше всего набрать на SAM, а затем сохранить на диск или кассету. При запуске загружается «specrom» и другие машинные подпрограммы, подключается следующая страница памяти, и SAM начинает работать как Spectrum. Это касается и клавиатуры, поэтому вам нужно помнить, какие клавиши соответствуют ключевым словам Spectrum. Я кладу рядом свою старую резиновую клавиатуру для подсказки. Если вы попытаетесь вызвать Mon16 (USR 30479), ничего не произойдет, потому что когда подключается страница 2 со specrom с адреса 0, выполнение начинается с этого адреса — то есть происходит сброс Спектрума. Первая часть этой подпрограммы очищает RAM до FFFFh. Таким образом, она стирает загруженные машинные коды. На самом деле она заполняет адреса двойками («2»), затем проверяет и заменяет их нулями.

Мы можем предотвратить это, модифицировав ПЗУ, поскольку сейчас оно находится в ОЗУ. (Да, мы заодно можем избавиться и от всех этих старых багов!). Требуемая модификация — это команда перехода в обход процедуры очистки RAM CLEAR. Она заносится первым же poke в строке 30 (JP 4555).

Теперь подпрограммы в машинных кодах не теряются, и команда RANDOMISE USR 30479 вызывает монитор, позволяя дизассемблировать и просматривать ПЗУ SAM или любую другую последовательность кодов (или выполнять её в пошаговом режиме и т. д.).

Таким же способом я загрузил и запустил ассемблер «EDITAS». А также одну игру (единственную, которая у меня есть!).

2. БЕЙСИК-ПРОГРАММЫ. Оказавшись в режиме Спектрума, все программы можно загружать с ленты и запускать обычным образом. Собственно, этот текст я пишу в Tasword 2 на SAM. Вы вполне резонно спросите: «Зачем тогда загружать программы так, как описано в первой части?». Ответ прост: их можно загружать прямо с диска.

3. Если бы можно было переключаться обратно в SAM без потери данных на верхних страницах... Тогда было бы легко использовать диск для сохранения текстов или других данных, созданных в режиме Спектрума. Это наверняка возможно, но я пока не догадался, как именно.
```text
SAVE "name" CODE 23552,(PEEK 23641 + 256 * PEEK 23642 - 23552)
```

Затем это можно загрузить в SAM, сохранить на диск и загружать строкой:

```text
30 LOAD "name" CODE 65536+23552
```
(Строку 40, конечно, нужно удалить).

Загвоздка здесь в том, что запуск «specrom» (при переключении страниц) сбрасывает системные переменные к их начальным значениям. Думаю, с этим можно справиться, если загружать данные по какому-нибудь более высокому адресу, а затем перемещать их вниз уже в режиме Спектрума. В системе есть приятные мелочи: например, можно вывести обычный каталог на экран командой DIR, а по DIR1 получить расширенный вариант, где распечатываются адреса начала/длины кодовых блоков и автозапуск Бейсика. Если вы сохраняете файл под уже существующим именем, машина спрашивает «OVERWRITE Y/N». Временами это раздражает, но пару раз уже спасло меня от затирания нужного файла. В общем и целом — вполне удобная система для жизни.

### Новости о SAM от Brian для всех

Многие будущие статьи, посвященные именно SAM, возможно, будут появляться только в версии OUTLET для SAM (или, возможно, в ADD-ENDERS), но информация из этого письма актуальна и для пользователей Spectrum, ожидающих новостей об ошибках в SAM, загрузке с ленты и т.д., прежде чем купить SAM.

Как уже должно быть известно большинству пользователей SAM, новая версия ROM теперь разослана текущим владельцам и устанавливается на все новые компьютеры. Свяжитесь с MGT, если вы еще не получили свою.

В итоге MGT решила разослать микросхему ROM нынешним владельцам SAM для самостоятельной установки, предоставив возможность обратиться к дилеру, если пользователь не уверен в своих силах. Инструкции по установке были очень четкими и точными, и я считаю, что они приняли правильное решение.

На момент написания этих строк новое ПЗУ у меня всего несколько дней, так что приведенные ниже подробности — результат далеко не исчерпывающего тестирования: к этому же времени в следующем месяце какие-то моменты могут проясниться, а могут вылезти и новые серьезные ошибки. Впрочем, я почти уверен, что не обнаружится ничего критического, чего нельзя было бы обойти.

Рад сообщить, что все серьезные ошибки были устранены;

остались одна-две странности и причуды, а также я обнаружил ошибку, которая для меня в новинку (хотя кто-то говорит, что она присутствовала и в старом ROM). Надеюсь, ее можно исправить с помощью POKE, так как дело, возможно, всего лишь в неверно выставляемом флаге.

С нее и начну. Если вы загружаетесь с кассеты или используете `DEVICE T`, `LOAD ""` а затем нажимаете ESC и вводите `DEVICE D`, команда BOOT перестает работать — как при нажатии F9, так и при вводе команды BOOT вручную. Вместо этого дисковод жужжит, а затем SAM переходит в режим ожидания загрузки с ленты. Если после этого загрузить что-то с дисковода с помощью обычной команды LOAD, то дальше все вроде бы работает нормально — что, как я и говорил, указывает на сброс флага в правильное состояние. К сожалению, если вы этого НЕ сделаете, SAM вскоре намертво зависает — скажем, после ввода пары строк и команды LIST. Из-за этого я просто не успевал поработать с клавиатурой достаточно долго, чтобы выявить точную причину!

Этот сбой воспроизводится абсолютно стабильно, и мне не верится, что никто из команды MGT не заметил его за месяцы тестирования. Если кто-то найдет решение, пожалуйста, дайте знать. Пока же я рекомендую использовать в программах `LOAD "AUTO*"` для перехода к загрузочному файлу.

Прежде чем перейти к менее значительным странностям, давайте взглянем на положительные стороны. SAM COUPE теперь — это ВЕРШИНА эволюции Spectrum. У него есть потрясающие возможности, которые за последние несколько месяцев оказались в тени. Дело не только в мощной графике, более быстром BASIC и дополнительных командах; не только в улучшенной клавиатуре, сверхбыстрых дисководах и более удобном системном разъеме; не только в кардинально улучшенном звуке и видеорежимах — радость для программиста на BASIC кроется в мелочах:
Функциональные клавиши — достаточно нажать ВСЕГО ОДНУ кнопку, чтобы выполнить RUN, LIST, CLS или BOOT. Более того, вы можете переназначать их по своему вкусу. Мгновенное редактирование: набираете номер строки и жмете EDIT — какая благодать! Клавиша TAB, мгновенно дающая отступ там, где нужно! Попробуйте поставить штук шесть после END PROC или RETURN, и вы увидите, как это помогает визуально структурировать листинг. На Spectrum для КАЖДОЙ табуляции приходилось нажимать EXTENDED MODE, клавишу 6 и DELETE. Кнопка BREAK, спасающая даже при многих сбоях в машинном коде — настоящее спасение!

В BASIC потрясающий потенциал дает KEYIN, а также функции MEM$ и поиск с помощью INSTR. Однако истинная жемчужина этого BASIC — процедуры, реализованные просто идеально: они позволяют МГНОВЕННО СОЗДАВАТЬ НОВЫЕ КЛЮЧЕВЫЕ СЛОВА ПРЯМО НА ХОДУ! Попробуйте вот это...

```text
10 SETUP
20 PRINTMENU
30 TESTKEY
40 HAVEAPARTY
```

Нужна специальная подпрограмма печати? Просто напишите `SPECPRINT "TEXT"`, а затем создайте процедуру, которая, скажем, переключает набор символов, меняет цвет INK, включает двойную высоту, печатает вашу строку, а затем возвращает все в исходное состояние! Возможности для творческого программиста просто колоссальные!

Теперь я чувствую себя увереннее и с загрузкой с ленты, разобравшись с уровнями сигнала, хотя с некоторыми коммерческими программами для Spectrum все еще могут возникать сложности.

Если вы раздумывали о покупке SAM COUPE, больше не сомневайтесь! В этом или следующем номере OUTLET у нас будет эмулятор Spectrum, который запускает большинство программ для Spectrum — их можно остановить в любой момент, сохранить на диск, ленту или даже в ramdisc, а с помощью BASIC эмулятор легко модифицировать, чтобы, скажем, сохранять текстовые файлы Tasword 2 на диск или выводить их на принтер.

Хорошо. А теперь вернемся к странностям...

Копирование файлов с одним дисководом дает сбой в Mode 1 или 2. Решение: используйте Mode 3 или 4.

FORMAT для "D2:" завершается ошибкой в Mode 1 или 2. Решение: используйте Mode 3 или 4.

Загрузка с ленты срывается, если позиция PRINT достигает низа экрана (например, когда я переношу все файлы OUTLET со Spectrum!). Решение: используйте SCROLL CLEAR.

DUMP и DUMP CHR$ требуют загрузки дополнительного кода, но пользователям ленты он недоступен, так что вы не сможете использовать DUMP в программах, которыми делитесь, да и MGT не объясняет новичкам, как внедрять его В программы.

DUMP CHR$ работает нормально — но ничуть не лучше, чем TEEDEE в OUTLET 33 (так что для большинства задач вы, возможно, предпочтете просто объединить TEEDEE).

DUMP разочаровывает. Все цветные экраны, что я пробовал, распечатались как невнятные черные пятна — будто любой цвет, кроме белого, печатается черным. Единственный успех был с черно-белым экраном клипарта. GEEDEE (OUTLET 33) работает медленно, но дает лучшие результаты. Решение: ждите сторонний DUMP — возможно, прямо в OUTLET!

OVER 1 ведет себя так, как ранее сообщалось в OUTLET. Решение: для всех практических целей считайте его исключительно командой Mode 1.

Функциональная клавиша F7 при включении по-прежнему не переключает устройство Device T на загрузку с ленты. Решение: переопределите эту клавишу в самом часто используемом файле.

DVAR 2, хранящая данные о дисководе 2 — параметр, с которым нужно быть начеку. Мне говорили, что на однодисководных COUPE происходит жуткий сбой, если отдается команда для дисковода 2, а DVAR 2 настроена на 2 привода. Пользователям с одним дисководом следует помнить об этом при загрузке с незнакомого диска. Я полагал, что BOOT проверяет, загружен ли уже DOS, но, похоже, он загружает DOS заново каждый раз при запуске файла автозагрузки. Это значит, что при загрузке с нового диска вы теряете все переменные дисководов. Например, если у вас DOS настроен на один дисковод, вы присылаете программу на диске, а я загружаю ее для проверки, то через десять минут могу внезапно обнаружить, что мой второй дисковод не работает! DOS на дисках OUTLET настроен (и должен быть настроен) на два дисковода, потому что во многих программах есть выбор для загрузки данных и т. д., и я совершенно не намерен ограничивать владельцев двух приводов использованием только одного! Например, CATLOADER (OUTLET 33) умеет перемещать файлы как на одном диске, так и между двумя. (К слову, диск от MGT, хоть и определил наличие двух дисководов, при создании резервной копии все равно предложил копирование только на одном приводе!). Это наводит на мысль: в той программе есть подпрограмма определения количества установленных дисководов, так что, возможно, было бы разумно использовать ее в файле автозагрузчика OUTLET AUTO.

Тут явно есть над чем подумать. Некоторые уже выпущенные программы OUTLET не работают с новым ROM, и мне придется протестировать их все, чтобы выяснить, что сломалось и почему! Жаль, что последствия нам приходится расхлебывать самостоятельно. Пишите, если обнаружите какую-нибудь полезную информацию.

Например, мультипалитра SCREEN$ "pal$" (OUTLET 33), сохраненная со старыми DOS и ROM, зависнет при попытке загрузить ее под новым ROM и DOS. Надо не забыть поместить исправленную версию в этот номер.
